research-methods-experiment.alt: Sixty volunteers are randomly assigned, by a coin flip, to two groups. The experimental group gets the real treatment, one level of the independent variable; the control group gets a placebo, a look-alike with no active ingredient. Both groups are then measured on the dependent variable as it is operationally defined, and the groups are compared: because only the treatment differed, a difference points to cause and effect. A side note explains double-blind: neither the participants nor the researchers who measure them know who is in which group.
